text: Giving to charity is important. Be careful of 'professional beggars'. People who are trapped are those who can't emigrate to earn a living. Rashad explains his encounter with 'professional beggars'.  ...retribution of karma with karma and whatever you put out will come back to you and more.  And in one sense you can guide people, but if you are, you're only doing so in the sense that you're an instrument of God's will.  And this reminds me of yasin, which I've been reading a lot. Whether you warn them or you warn them not, they will not believe.  So people who are going to believe will believe, and people who aren't going to believe aren't going to believe.  You may be there as an intermediary, you may be the first one to stick the Koran in their hand, but it's not in their heart to believe it.  They're not going to believe it anyway. So it's basically, again, all power is to God.  Charity shall go to the poor who are persecuted because of their belief and trapped.  Those who are unaware may think that they are rich due to their honorable character, but you can recognize them by certain signs.  They never annoy the people by begging, and any charity you give God is fully aware of.  Those who give charity by name and by deed, secretly and publicly, their recompense is with the Lord.  They have nothing to fear, nor will they grieve.  In Morocco there are people who bug you about charity.  They're professional beggars. They may not even be poor.  I vividly remember one woman in Marrakesh who could cry at will.  She would come up and, you know, whether her husband was just lazy and they had money,  and just said, go out and beg if you want something, and maybe they had money.  Whereas you just see people there just sitting reciting something from the Koran,  not even thinking about charity, and people would throw that money.  It's a good illustration. I've seen both kinds.  some of them, are very rich. Some of them died and found ...  They are professional beggars. That's the point/  So it's basically more about the laws of charity.  People who are persecuted because of their belief and trapped.  So I'm just again saying that charity is a good thing, and it's one of the five pillars,  and it explains a little bit more about life.  These three lines are about...  These three items are about charity.  The poor who are persecuted for their belief and trapped.  What does that mean in Arabic?  They can't immigrate or move to another place where they can earn a living.  Some people are trapped in their properties and can't move around.  I just think of all the people who I've seen chanting,  and one man who I remember had the most beautiful voice,  and he would just stand in the street and recite from the Koran, he was blind.  It didn't seem like he ever wanted charity.  People would feed him, and they would give him what he wanted.  It didn't seem like he cared or not.  He just felt really good when you gave something to him.  Then there were these professional beggars who would just go around.  I like that phrase.  They'd just go around, and you didn't know if they were really...  I suppose if you were a tourist and you didn't live there very long,  you wouldn't really know for sure.  On the other hand, if you've ever been to Marrakesh,  you know that if you feed all the beggars in Marrakesh,  you'll be a beggar yourself.  In Morocco and in the East, begging is not illegal.  It's actually something that people do professionally.  I think these three verses are making a distinction.  Here you can't just go around and ask people for money for a handout.  Your considered a bum or a transient or something like that.  You can be arrested for beggarcy or something like that.  Just the predominance of begging, alright?  It's not very predominant in this country compared to...  It's just not very predominant to see people standing around on the street with a...  normally their they don't have a social security or a welfare or  You'll see another guy showing his stump off.  Make sure you see it.  Somebody walks up to you and shows you that he doesn't have any arms.  It's a different...  so these professional beggars will actually cut their ..  It's really the people who are persecuted because of what they believe that deserves charity the most.  You can recognize it by their signs, okay?  They never annoy people by begging.  These beggars can be very, very much of a nuisance.  you think that beggars in Morocco should go to India  and they can be champion runners I can tell you that. I remember I was riding in-whats the name of those carts that people pull?  Rickshaw right? There was a Rickshaw pulled by a motorcycle... and the streets were crowded, and I must have had like 12 beggars following me  wherever I go  Very fast.  No, no, no, no, no, no, no, no.  The boys are extending their hand, you know, they're beggars.  Then I get in the rickshaw and the driver goes very fast.  And the 12 boys are still around with the rickshaw.  And then he'd go really fast.  And we'd get rid of the horses for about a minute.  And then he'd slow down a little bit just a minute.  And then the 12 again.  They run for an hour after the pitch, they're very fast.  Really, I mean they can win marathons and make millions  of dollars in this country.  But that's nothing compared to the Moroccans.  And now Egypt, we had lots of beggars, ...  and he wiped out that disease. He put them all in jail.  I mean,  he didn't give them any help.  He was that kind  of dictator.  No more beggars in Egypt, put them all in prison.  That's what they do.  My favorite thing is  you're playing a musical instrument while you're a street  entertainer. You just walk around on the street, get a dime,  you know, a quarter, five dollars.  I think they're a pretty good group.  San Francisco is full of people who are actually entertainers, like you said.  Very talented entertainers.  Some of them was up from a hundred feet up  into a can of water.  You understand this one?  I mean, they're risking their lives, but they really have to play it.  What's this?  Some musicians.  Musicians. Really talented. Last updated 11 months ago
